phrase.text: This specification describes the whole PseudoLearn language and its engine, with examples that really run every time it is built.

runs.text: This specification describes the whole PseudoLearn language and its engine, with examples that really run every time it is built.

The specification is divided into thirteen parts and six appendices. Each part covers a topic and each section explains a single idea. You can read it from start to finish or jump straight to what you need.
The parts follow the order in which people usually learn to program. First the loose pieces of the text, then data, then instructions, and finally how the engine works inside.

runs.text: Every program in this specification was run with the real PseudoLearn engine. Below each one you see what it wrote and how it ended. If the engine ever changed its behaviour, the specification would stop building until the text was corrected.
Every section has a body that makes sense without prior knowledge. Around the body there are boxes you can read or skip:

rows.text: The idea of the section summed up in one sentence
The precise number when it matters: ranges, sizes, depths
The real engine messages and how to fix them
What the engine does: intermediate representation and trace
Typical confusions and questions for the class

runs.text: The body never depends on the collapsible boxes. You can skip every "Inside" without losing the thread.
This specification explains the language to people. It is not a step-by-step course: the learning path is for that. Nor is it the internal description of the engine's code.

points.text: Thirteen parts ordered from small to large and six reference appendices.
One idea per section, with a figure, run examples and a summary.
Every example was run with the engine when the specification was built.
